title: Fallout Episode 5's Easter Eggs Include A Throwback To The First Game’s Villain
description: This week’s venture into the Mojave Wasteland really hit home the idea that a lot of stories in the Fallout universe are intrinsically connected. From events that took place before the Great War, to events of the video games and the current timeline of the show, there’s no shortage of connections that form a deep and intricate web. With that in mind, let’s dive into some of the more notable points and easter eggs from episode five. A Fragmented Strip The Strip in Fallout: New VegasAs Lucy (Ella Purnell) and Cooper (Walton Goggins) explore The Strip and Freeside, the pair come to discover that the region is divided into sections by chainlink fences. These fences turn the strip from a massive throughstreet into smaller areas, akin to the level design from Fallout: New Vegas. While most may think this may have been an aesthetic choice, in actuality Obsidian Entertainment had to implement these fences because the game’s engine kept crashing when The Strip was a single large area. Talk about making the most of a bad situation. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Modder Combines PS5, Xbox Series X, And Switch 2 Into A Single Machine
description: Microsoft's "Everything is an Xbox" approach may have sent formerly Xbox-exclusive games to the PlayStation 5, but it's far from a two-way street. And it would take some kind of gaming miracle to get Nintendo to loan out its Switch franchises to other systems. But one gamer had the impossible dream of bringing an Xbox Series X, a PS5, and Switch 2 into a single machine, and she did it. The Ningtendo PXBOX 5 was created by 小宁子 XNZ, who shared the video above late last year (via GamesRadar). While the video is in Chinese, English subtitles are encoded for fans who want to follow the process. As XNZ explains in the video, she noticed that the consoles look very similar once they've been removed from their casings. The motherboards only take up a relatively small space, while the cooling system and power supply require a much larger area. XNZ's solution was to create a custom container inspired by the 2013 Mac Pro "trash can" design. Through trial and error, she came up with a three-sided internal design that allowed the motherboards to be situated on each side of the cooling system while sharing a single 250W PC power supply. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Razer Boss Decries AI "Slop" But Is Still Bullish On AI In Games
description: During this year's CES, Razer declared that the "future of gaming is AI," which led to a backlash on the company's social media channels. Razer CEO Min-Liang Tan hasn't backed down from his company's stance, but he has offered an explanation that clarifies where it stands on AI in game development. "'What are we unhappy with?' When I say we, I mean us as gamers," Tan told The Verge. "I think we're unhappy with generative AI slop, right? Just to put it out there. And that's something that I'm unhappy with. Like any gamer, when I play a game, I want to be engaged, I wanna be immersed, I wanna be able to be competitive. I don't want to be served character models with extra fingers and stuff like that, or shoddily written storylines, so on and so forth. I think for us, we're all aligned against gen AI slop that is just churned out from a couple of prompts and stuff like that." Tan went on to state that AI tools can be used to help developers fix bugs and complete games faster without resorting to using AI slop as content. He also noted that he's against AI "replacing human creativity." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: WoW Mods Are Changing Forever Today
description: World of Warcraft: Midnight's expansion pre-patch is out later today on January 20, and once it's live, many of the game's player-made mods for assisting in combat (add-ons) will look and function much differently than before. In some cases, they may not even work at all. Announced early last year, Blizzard is finally ripping off the combat add-on Band-Aid today in an effort to make WoW more understandable out of the box and make it so add-ons don't offer distinct advantages in combat. For well over a decade, players doing endgame raids or high-level Mythic+ dungeons have always relied on combat add-ons to make the game easier to parse. Sometimes that meant specific boss callouts or solutions for certain boss mechanics. Other times it meant custom reminders on when to use specific abilities. That's changing come pre-patch. Many of the add-ons that have over the years essentially become required for playing WoW competently, like the damage meter Details! and encounter-helper add-on Deadly Boss Mods, will instead be baked into WoW's own default user interface. It should, in theory, raise the floor for all WoW players, who now will all have a baseline UI to work from that offers much of the important information add-ons used to provide. Combined with Blizzard's encounter design efforts to make it so add-ons aren't required in order to succeed, WoW's endgame will likely feel much different than in years past. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Developer's Office Rocked By An Explosion
description: Rockstar North, the development studio behind Grand Theft Auto 6, was struck by an explosion earlier this week at its office in Edinburgh, Scotland. The explosion occurred at 5:02 AM local time on January 19, and it apparently took place in the facility's boiler room. According to BNO News, the incident set off a small fire at Rockstar North's office, and emergency response crews were on the scene for four hours. No injuries were reported from the fire or explosion, and Rockstar issued a statement that thanked the first responders and assured fans that GTA 6 development wasn't affected. "Many thanks to those that reached out with concern, and also to the police and fire crews who were on scene quickly to access the situation. Please know that everyone is well and our studio remains open and operational." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Life Is Strange: Reunion Finally Brings Back Chloe Price
description: Deck Nine and Square Enix have officially revealed Life is Strange: Reunion after a tease last week and an Xbox Wire leak earlier today. It's out in March and is meant to serve as the culmination and conclusion of Max Caulfield and Chloe Price's story. Yes, Chloe Price is returning in Life is Strange: Reunion after not appearing in 2024's Double Exposure, to the chagrin of the series' fan base. It'll follow the pair as they reunite following Max's merging of realities at the end of Double Exposure and Chloe's time either being dead or serving as a tour manager for a band called Drugstore Makeup. A fire is seemingly destined to destroy Caledon University, where Max has settled down. The key to preventing that (and some more cataclysmic events in the future) will force Max and Chloe to reunite and work together. The stream featuring the game's announcement trailer revealed more, like the fact that it will account for whether or not players decided to let Chloe die at the end of the original. Continue Reading at GameSpot
